PMID:42719498.topic: Marker ball positioning for hip arthroplasty templating
PMID:42719498.setting: York District Hospital (York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust), trauma hip arthroplasty for intracapsular neck of femur fractures
PMID:42719498.standard: Departmental audit standard: 100% of pre-operative pelvic radiographs should contain a correctly positioned marker ball (fully visible, inferior to the pubic symphysis, equidistant between the femora at the level of the greater trochanters)

cycle1.result: Marker ball present and fully visible in 96.2% (50/52). Mean difference between templated and implanted head size 2.82 mm (range −5 to +11 mm); 24 (48%) larger, 18 (36%) smaller, 6 (12%) same size.

PMID:42719498.intervention: Results presented at departmental audit meeting; 30-minute teaching session for radiology staff on marker ball placement and educational posters displayed in the radiology department.

cycle2.result: Marker ball present in 93.0% (40/43); present and fully visible in 86.0% (37/43). Mean difference between templated and implanted head size fell to 1.51 mm (range −4 to +7 mm), p = 0.008; 16 (43%) larger, 12 (32%) smaller, 9 (24%) same size.

PMID:42719498.other_findings: Compliance with a fully visible marker ball fell from 96.2% to 86.0% despite improved templating accuracy. In the second cycle 19% of trauma hip arthroplasties were not templated and were excluded.

PMID:40821226.topic: Early weight bearing after ankle fracture fixation
PMID:40821226.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Royal Cornwall Hospital, Truro (district general hospital)
PMID:40821226.standard: BOAST 12: early weight bearing after ankle fracture ORIF unless there is a documented concern about fixation stability or soft tissue condition

cycle1.result: 56/112 (50%) advised early weight bearing; 56 (50%) advised delayed weight bearing without documented contraindications.

PMID:40821226.intervention: Findings presented at the audit meeting; BOAST guidelines disseminated by departmental email, educational posters displayed in clinical areas, and agreement on a structured rehabilitation pathway.

cycle2.result: 40/58 (69%) advised early weight bearing; 18 (31%) delayed. Absolute improvement 19% (95% CI 3.9%–34.1%), chi-square 5.591, p = 0.018; NNT 5.3.

PMID:40821226.other_findings: All cases had clearly documented postoperative weight-bearing instructions. Patient-reported and functional outcomes were not assessed.

PMID:41458349.topic: Distal radius fracture time to fixation
PMID:41458349.setting: Tertiary trauma centre, University Hospitals Dorset (Poole)
PMID:41458349.standard: NICE NG38 and BOAST: intra-articular distal radius fractures fixed within 72 hours and extra-articular within 7 days of presentation; target compliance 80%

cycle1.result: Intra-articular fixed within 72 hours 14/42 (33.3%), mean 6.0 ± 3.2 days; extra-articular fixed within 7 days 11/23 (48%; table gives 42%), mean 9.0 ± 4.1 days. Overall mean time to fixation 6.7 ± 3.7 days.

PMID:41458349.intervention: Appointment of a dedicated hand and wrist consultant and a protected Thursday trauma list for upper limb fractures.

cycle2.result: Intra-articular within 72 hours 23/55 (42%); extra-articular within 7 days 12/19 (63%), mean 6.4 ± 3.0 days. Overall mean time to fixation 5.3 ± 2.8 days (p = 0.03).

PMID:41458349.other_findings: The paper reports conflicting p values for compliance change (p = 0.04 and 0.02 in text; p = 0.38 and 0.27 in Table 3). Both standards remained below the 80% target.

PMID:28405534.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, St James's Hospital, Dublin (inpatient orthopaedic operations)
PMID:28405534.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice (2014) operation note headings

cycle1.dates: April to October 2014 (previous audit of handwritten notes)
cycle1.result: Handwritten notes: tourniquet time 0%, elective/emergency 0%, duration 1.6%, operative diagnosis 74.6%, incision 81.7%, prosthesis named 79.6%, serial numbers 30%; 14% of 57 handwritten notes judged illegible.

PMID:28405534.intervention: Typed operation notes on the standard hospital proforma, with an added tourniquet time heading for orthopaedic notes.

cycle2.result: Typed notes: procedure name, incision, closure, tourniquet time and postoperative instructions 100%; elective/emergency 100%; duration 63.2%; operative diagnosis 80.7%; prosthesis named 98.2%; serial numbers 26.9%; 100% legible.

PMID:28405534.other_findings: Prosthesis serial numbers remained poorly documented (26.9% vs 30%). Postoperative instructions were in the correct place only 30.5% of the time.

PMID:39176321.topic: Orthogeriatric review of older trauma patients
PMID:39176321.setting: Orthopaedic department, Countess of Chester Hospital or Wythenshawe Hospital (not specified); patients aged 65 or over with fragility fractures and stay over 72 hours
PMID:39176321.standard: BOAST care of the older or frail orthopaedic trauma patient: comprehensive geriatric assessment by a geriatrician within 72 hours of injury; physiotherapy on postoperative day 1

cycle1.dates: 8 September 2022 to 8 March 2023 (plus non-hip fracture admissions 8 March to 8 May 2023)
cycle1.result: Geriatrician review within 72 hours in 37/70 (52.9%): hip fracture 31/39 (79.5%) vs non-hip fracture 6/31 (19.3%), p<0.001. Mean geriatrician reviews 15 vs 5 (p<0.001).

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:39176321.other_findings: Physiotherapy on day 1 after surgery: 30/36 (83%) hip fracture vs 8/16 (50%) non-hip fracture (p>0.05). No significant difference in length of stay or 30-day mortality.

PMID:41211261.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics department, University Hospital Crosshouse, NHS Ayrshire and Arran (elective and emergency cases)
PMID:41211261.standard: GMC Good Medical Practice and RCS Good Surgical Practice operative note parameters; target 100%

cycle1.result: Typed 25 (30%); operative diagnosis 53 (65%); findings 60 (73%); closure 73 (89%); signature 78 (95%); prosthesis identification 60/69 (87%); estimated blood loss 5 (6%); time 12%; trauma/elective 27%.

PMID:41211261.intervention: Theatre posters of documentation standards, encouragement to use typed or templated notes, and a mandatory post-operative checklist before leaving recovery.

cycle2.result: Typed 55 (65%, p<0.001); closure 84 (100%, p=0.038); signature 84 (100%, p=0.040); operative diagnosis 62 (74%); findings 68 (81%); prosthesis identification 47/54 (87%); estimated blood loss 2 (2%).

PMID:41211261.other_findings: Time (11%) and trauma/elective status (24%) stayed poor. Re-audit was only a month after the first cycle.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.474.setting: Mental Health and Learning Disabilities division, ABUHB (acute psychiatric wards and psychiatric intensive care unit)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.474.standard: NMC guidance on verbal orders (follow-up written instruction by a doctor)

cycle1.result: Round 1 survey of 26 nurses and 27 doctors: e.g. 19% of nurses would request haloperidol without a recent ECG and 8% of doctors would prescribe it; 12% of nurses and 12.5% of doctors would request/prescribe lorazepam above BNF maximum doses.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.474.intervention: Verbal orders replaced by a digital order form completed by the ward nurse with prompts (medication, physical health, QTc, vital signs) and emailed back by the doctor; publicised via email, junior doctor forums and induction.

cycle2.result: Round 2 survey of 8 nurses and 8 doctors: 100% of nurses familiar with the digital forms; 75% of nurses said the form puts up barriers and 87.5% found it more time consuming; 6 doctors rated the new system safer.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.474.other_findings: Main measurement was an opinion survey rather than compliance data. Nurses were less positive than doctors, with 3 of 8 wishing to revert to verbal orders.

PMID:26357669.setting: Orthopaedic inpatients, St James's Hospital, Dublin (standard handwritten operation sheet)
PMID:26357669.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice (2008) operation note guidelines

cycle1.result: Date and time, surgeon, procedure and signature 100%; operative diagnosis 74.6% (in designated place 63.8%); incision 81.7%; closure 98.3%; postoperative instructions 96.3% (41% in wrong place); tourniquet time 0%; prosthesis serial numbers 30%; elective/emergency 0%.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:26357669.other_findings: 85.7% of notes were written by the registrar although consultants performed 71.4% of procedures. Authors planned re-audit after introduction of electronic notes.

PMID:32821626.setting: Orthopaedic department, Ribat University Hospital, Khartoum (tertiary care hospital)
PMID:32821626.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice (2014) operation note criteria, with added orthopaedic items (19 items)

cycle1.result: Good compliance for date (86%), diagnosis (85%), operating surgeon (90%), assistants (86%), procedure (98%), post-operative instructions (98%), signature (75%). Poor: time 37%, anaesthetist 41%, incision 41%, prosthesis details 15%, drain 7%.

PMID:32821626.intervention: Memory aid placed in the operating theatre for two months (May–June 2019) highlighting poorly documented items.

cycle2.result: Time 56%, anaesthetist 46%, incision 59%, prosthesis size and details 34%, drain documented in correct place 15%.

PMID:32821626.other_findings: Notes written by the operating surgeon fell from 20% to 14%. Some components remained poorly completed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.76.topic: Physical health checks in substance misuse services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.76.setting: Gwent Specialist Substance Misuse Services (GSSMS), North Team

cycle1.result: Physical examination by GSSMS 60/121; ECG 37/121 (31%); blood-borne virus screen in last 6 months 62/121. Abnormality found in 77% of those examined, most commonly hypertension (9) and abdominal tenderness (9).

cycle2.result: not reported

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.76.other_findings: Physical examination rates were described as having risen from 0% to 50% compared with previous practice, and the team previously had no ECG machine. A front-of-notes checklist and yearly re-audit were recommended.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11800.topic: Mental Health Act medical recommendation quality
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11800.setting: South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust, Wakefield area (section 2 and 3 medical recommendations)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11800.standard: Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice and statutory forms; 100% compliance expected on 8 standards

cycle1.dates: Recommendations from January 2025 onwards; data collected August to September 2025
cycle1.result: 100% for stating mental disorder, describing symptoms, nature or degree, own health reasons and why informal admission inappropriate; own safety reasons 62%; protection of others 81%; why community treatment not available 90%.

cycle2.result: not reported

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11800.other_findings: Sample contained only section 3 and single recommendations. Feedback to doctors and an agreed template were proposed, with re-audit planned in three to six months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11255.topic: Admission clerking and physical health checks in psychiatric inpatients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11255.setting: Battersea Bridge House Hospital, 22-bed acute mental health facility (three wards)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11255.standard: Local and NHS trust admission protocol: clerking, mental state examination, physical examination, ECG and routine bloods all completed within 72 hours of admission

cycle1.result: All five criteria completed within 72 hours in 27 patients (62.8%); delayed in 14 (33.6%); 2 (4.7%) refused blood tests.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11255.intervention: Active physical health handover to the physical health nurse and junior doctors, with emphasis on patient rapport.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance for physical health checks increased from 62.4% to 96.6% after intervention; reported 1.76-fold increase in timely protocol completion, 1.39-fold reduction in delays and 4-fold drop in patient refusal.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11255.other_findings: Delays were mainly due to patient agitation, refusal of bloods or ECG, delayed consent and slow laboratory results; reasons were not documented for 2 patients.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.099.setting: Specialist HPB multidisciplinary team, University Hospitals Plymouth; patients referred locally from Plymouth Hospitals NHS Trust
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.099.standard: NHS standard: first definitive treatment within 62 days of urgent GP referral

cycle1.result: Median time from first presentation to surgery 0 days (range 189); to first chemotherapy 81 days (range 231); to palliative decision 23 days (range 77). Delays: presentation to SMDT referral via GP median 9 days (range 17); referral to first discussion median 9 (range 53); first discussion to first biopsy median 31 (range 165).

cycle2.result: not reported

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.099.other_findings: Median of 2 SMDT discussions per patient (range 7). Preliminary data suggest patients wait longer than NHS guidelines; proportion meeting the 62-day target not reported.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10566.setting: Medical wards, CDU and UTC, Friarage Hospital, Northallerton; patients over 65 referred to psychiatric liaison

cycle1.result: 22/38 (58%) had delirium documented during admission; of these 13 (59%) had delirium documented in the discharge letter and 9 (41%) had no mention. By ward: Romanby 2/8 (25%), Ainderby 5/6 (83%), Rutson 0/1, CDU/UTC 6/7 (86%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10566.intervention: Planned: teaching for Foundation Year doctors, ward posters from 08/01/25, and encouraging documentation of previous delirium at clerking.

cycle2.result: not reported

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10566.other_findings: First cycle only; re-audit planned for March 2025 using February 2025 discharges.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.377.topic: ADHD in early intervention for psychosis
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.377.setting: Early intervention for psychosis service, Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 5/174 (2.9%) adult patients had a known ADHD diagnosis; 4 more referred for ADHD assessment.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.377.intervention: Development of an integrated clinical pathway and NICE-concordant care plan for ADHD in the EIP service, with the adult ADHD service.

cycle2.result: not reported

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.377.other_findings: A previous 2022 audit found 3.6% prevalence of diagnosed ADHD. Adult ADHD assessment waiting list is 18 months to 2 years; 3/5 patients had a history of substance use.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.190.setting: Delfryn House, high dependency inpatient mental health rehabilitation unit
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.190.standard: Safe prescription and administration of psychotropic medication; Mental Health Act 1983 treatment certificate compliance

cycle1.result: Phase I: prescription errors 19%; administration errors 34%; Mental Health Act documentation compliance 77%; patient knowledge of medication 15%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.190.intervention: Medication management committee with PDSA cycles: inpatient depot clinics, daily 10-point nurse self-audit, medication compliance in handovers, monthly prescription, administration and pharmacist audits, patient leaflets and pharmacist sessions, staff policy awareness and monthly MHA certificate audits.

cycle2.result: Phase II: prescription errors 3%; administration errors 11%; Mental Health Act documentation compliance 98%; patient knowledge 32%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.190.other_findings: Acknowledgement of drug interactions and adverse events raised by pharmacists did not improve significantly. Depot errors fell then rose again and the weekly depot clinic was abandoned.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.024.topic: Secondary prevention and carotid imaging after minor stroke
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.024.setting: Stroke ward E58, Sunderland Royal Hospital (South Tyneside and Sunderland Foundation Trust); patients with NIHSS score below 5
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.024.standard: National Clinical Guideline for Stroke: carotid Doppler ultrasound for TIA or minor anterior stroke (NIHSS below 5), with correct antiplatelet and statin therapy and lifestyle advice

cycle1.result: Cholesterol-lowering therapy about 3 percentage points lower and lifestyle advice 2 points lower than cycle 2; blood pressure commented on in only 3% of cases.

cycle2.result: Correct antiplatelet therapy 100%; cholesterol-lowering therapy 25/30 (83.3%); diet and lifestyle advice 4/30 (13.3%); blood pressure commented on 18/30 (60%). Only one patient had vascular surgery and not within seven days.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.024.other_findings: Ultrasound only available Monday to Friday 9:00–17:00, so weekend admissions cannot have a scan within 24 hours. Recommended adding carotid Doppler within 24 hours to ward induction.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.158.setting: Hepatobiliary department, University Hospital Southampton (elective and emergency splenectomy)
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.158.standard: National and local guidelines on post-splenectomy vaccination (Pneumovax, MenACWY, Bexsero, influenza) and antibiotic prophylaxis; 100% compliance expected

cycle1.result: Did not receive: Pneumovax 21%, Bexsero 22%, ACWY 23%, second Bexsero 34%, yearly influenza 30%; 21% received no vaccinations; 1% no prophylactic antibiotics on discharge; 39% of discharge paperwork lacked vaccination timing documentation.

cycle2.result: not reported

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.158.other_findings: A follow-up documentation proforma was created and clear discharge documentation recommended, with re-audit planned for 2023. No patients were readmitted with overwhelming infection.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.122.setting: 13 rheumatology outpatient departments in Greater Manchester and Lancashire (North West regional audit)
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.122.standard: NICE, EULAR, BSR and MHRA gout guidelines

cycle1.result: Treat-to-target levels agreed in 49 (57%); cardiovascular risk tool used in 3 (3%); no patient with major cardiovascular disease on febuxostat; 16 (17%) no planned follow-up; 18 (78%) new patients appropriately referred; 15 (75%) started on first-line ULT; 11 (79%) allopurinol started at low dose; 10 (67%) given colchicine prophylaxis.

cycle2.result: not reported

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.122.other_findings: None of 12 patients with hypertension without heart failure on diuretics received advice to reduce or stop them. Clinic data would have allowed cardiovascular risk calculation in 13 (14%).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.069.topic: Vitamin D supplementation in older adults
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.069.setting: Acute medical patients over 65, Wexford General Hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.069.standard: Department of Health guidance 2020: adults over 65 should take 15 micrograms vitamin D daily

cycle1.result: 48% not on any vitamin D supplement; 64% insufficient (32% deficient), of whom 44% not on vitamin D; vitamin D result mentioned in 18% of discharge letters.

cycle2.result: not reported

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.069.other_findings: 30% presented with fractures, and 10% of those were not on vitamin D.
